options.name: address
options.description: Sets the host, network or port entries for the alias. When `type` is set to `host`, each entry must be a valid IP address or FQDN. When `type` is set to `network`, each entry must be a valid network CIDR or FQDN. When `type` is set to `port`, each entry must be a valid port or port range. You may also specify an existing alias's `name` as an entry to created nested aliases.

options.name: api_host
options.description: The hostname or IP address of the pfSense device.

options.name: api_key
options.description: An API key to use for authentication.

options.name: api_password
options.description: The password to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: api_port
options.description: The port number of the pfSense API.

options.name: api_protocol
options.description: The protocol to use when connecting to the pfSense API.

options.name: api_username
options.description: The username to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: descr
options.description: Sets a description to help specify the purpose or contents of the alias.

options.name: detail
options.description: Sets descriptions for each alias `address`. Values must match the order of the `address` value it relates to. For example, the first value specified here is the description for the first value specified in the `address` field. This value cannot contain

options.name: lookup_fields
options.description: The list of fields to use when looking up existing resources. This should be a list of field names that uniquely identify a resource.

options.name: name
options.description: Sets the name for the alias. This name must be unique from all other aliases.

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the resource should be present or absent.

options.name: type
options.description: Sets the type of alias this object will be. This directly impacts what values can be specified in the `address` field.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to validate SSL certificates when connecting to the API.
